yt.title: Counting 1 billion per second, a 64-bit counter lasts {c_y} years #Shorts
yt.description:
2^64 / 10^9 counts per second / 31,557,600 seconds per year (365.25 days) = {c_y} years. A 32-bit counter at the same rate: 2^32 / 10^9 = {c_s32} seconds. Computed in Python.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.narration: A computer counts one billion times every second. How long until its counter runs out?

scenes.label: for a 64-bit counter at 1 billion per second
scenes.narration: With sixty four bits, a counter can go past eighteen quintillion. At one billion per second, that lasts {c_y_say} years.
With only thirty two bits, the same counter would overflow in {c_s32_say} seconds.
Each extra bit doubles the range. That is why many systems now use sixty four bit counters for time and IDs. How fast could you overflow yours?
